mediasoup.security_level: media transport baseline high, application security implementation-dependent
key_points: SFU media server for WebRTC conferencing
Supports WebRTC and plain RTP input/output
Signaling agnostic, so authentication and authorization are application responsibilities
WebRTC transport uses ICE and DTLS procedures; SRTP parameters are supported for relevant transports
primary_risks: Weak room authorization in custom signaling
No application-level E2EE unless separately implemented

n8n.security_level: automation maturity high, self-hosted attack surface medium-high
primary_risks: Git node file read or RCE paths

recommended_controls: Pin n8n version and update promptly
Bind n8n to localhost or internal network
Use TLS reverse proxy for any external access
Disable community nodes unless explicitly reviewed
Restrict workflow creation and editing to trusted users
Exclude high-risk nodes when not needed
Set N8N_ENCRYPTION_KEY and protect stored credentials
Prune execution data and avoid storing sensitive payloads
Treat n8n itself as a monitored high-risk automation asset
implemented_workflow_controls: 401 rejected response for missing or invalid webhook token
Input length and numeric bound normalization
No raw request body reflection in webhook response
Risk scoring for ICE, DTLS, producer, consumer, ZAP, IP candidate, and unauthorized join signals
remaining_workflow_risks: Default demo token must be changed after import
Shared token does not prove payload integrity
Replay protection is limited to timestamp freshness scoring
Reverse proxy TLS and rate limiting are still required for any non-local exposure
Workflow editor permissions remain a high-impact trust boundary
